subject: implementer
reason: One service (WebApp), about 3 files: the orders page, a new client script and App.razor.
mode_reason: One service (WebApp), about 3 files: the orders page, a new client script and App.razor.

items.goal: On My orders, show each order's Date in the browser's own time zone, in the existing format MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss. Orders.razor renders each date as <time class="order-date" datetime="{UTC ISO-8601 round-trip, Kind forced to Utc}"> with the current UTC text as a fallback. A new src/WebApp/wwwroot/js/order-local-time.js, loaded in App.razor next to the other scripts, rewrites every such element into the local date and time (24-hour, zero-padded month/day/hour/min/sec). It runs on load, after Blazor enhanced navigation (enhancedload) and when streaming or OrdersRefreshOnStatusChange inserts or replaces rows (MutationObserver), without converting a value twice. Order number, total and status stay unchanged. No scenario fits: the verifier signs in as alice, places an order (Explorer 45L Backpack), then opens My orders with the browser time zone set to America/Chicago and to Asia/Tokyo.
items.modelReason: Small but needs care with the Blazor streaming and enhanced-navigation lifecycle and with UTC handling.
items.verifyReason: Visible behavior that depends on the browser's time zone; a verifier must set the browser time zone and read the page.

alternatives.option: Make the page interactive and read the time zone over JS interop
alternatives.reason: Changes the rendering mode for a display-only fix and makes the first paint wrong.

alternatives.option: Store the time zone in a cookie and convert on the server
alternatives.reason: Wrong on the first visit and when the cookie goes stale; more moving parts.
